title: The BJP and the Jana Sangh
subtitle: From the Jana Sangh through the Janata Party to the BJP · 1951 – today
subject: bjp
intro: The Bharatiya Janata Party has had three names. Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951 with RSS organisers such as Deendayal Upadhyaya, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L. K. Advani; it won 3 seats in the first general election. In 1977 the Jana Sangh merged into the Janata Party, which defeated Indira Gandhi after the Emergency. When the Janata Party broke apart over 'dual membership' of the RSS, its Jana Sangh members re-formed as the BJP in 1980. From 2 seats in 1984, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement took it to power under Vajpayee (1998–2004) and Narendra Modi (since 2014). The Janata Dal (1988) and JD(U) were separate parties, at times allies and at times rivals.

events.title: The Hindu Mahasabha is founded
events.summary: The Hindu Mahasabha is formed at the Kumbh Mela in Haridwar as an all-India body for Hindu political interests. Syama Prasad Mookerjee would lead it in the 1940s before breaking away.

events.title: Hedgewar founds the RSS
events.summary: On Vijayadashami K. B. Hedgewar starts the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in Nagpur, a volunteer body built on daily shakhas. Nearly every leader of the Jana Sangh and the BJP comes through it.

events.title: Golwalkar leads the RSS
events.summary: Hedgewar dies and M. S. Golwalkar becomes sarsanghchalak. He leads the RSS for 33 years and later lends organisers to the Jana Sangh.

events.title: RSS banned after Gandhi's murder
events.summary: Days after Nathuram Godse kills Gandhi, the government bans the RSS. The ban is lifted in July 1949. The episode convinces many in the RSS that they need a political party of their own.

events.title: Mookerjee quits Nehru's cabinet
events.summary: Syama Prasad Mookerjee, Industries minister in the first cabinet, resigns in protest at the Nehru–Liaquat Pact on minorities in India and Pakistan, which he sees as abandoning East Bengal's Hindus.

events.title: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh is founded
events.summary: Mookerjee launches the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in Delhi, with its election symbol the oil lamp (deepak). The RSS lends organisers including Deendayal Upadhyaya, Nanaji Deshmukh and the young Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

events.title: First general election: 3 seats
events.summary: In independent India's first election the Jana Sangh wins 3 of 489 Lok Sabha seats with 3.06% of the vote, plus 35 seats in state assemblies. All three winners beat a divided field: none gets half the vote. It is recognised as one of four national parties.

events.title: Mookerjee defies the Kashmir permit
events.summary: Campaigning against Article 370 and the permit needed to enter Jammu and Kashmir ('one country, two constitutions, two prime ministers, two flags will not do'), Mookerjee crosses into the state at Lakhanpur without a permit and is arrested. Ending Article 370 stays on the party's agenda for 66 years.

events.title: 1957 election: 4 seats
events.summary: The Jana Sangh wins 4 Lok Sabha seats. Vajpayee enters Parliament from Balrampur, where his Hindi oratory impresses Nehru.

events.title: 1962 election: 14 seats
events.summary: The Jana Sangh rises to 14 seats, strongest in the Hindi heartland, Delhi and Punjab.

events.title: Integral Humanism
events.summary: In four lectures in Bombay, Deendayal Upadhyaya sets out Integral Humanism: an Indian path between capitalism and communism rooted in dharma. The Jana Sangh adopts it as doctrine, and the BJP still calls it its philosophy.

events.title: 1967: 35 seats and coalition governments
events.summary: Congress loses eight states. The Jana Sangh wins 35 Lok Sabha seats and enters Samyukta Vidhayak Dal coalitions with socialists and others in states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh — its first taste of power.

events.title: Deendayal Upadhyaya found dead
events.summary: Weeks after becoming president at the Calicut session, Deendayal Upadhyaya is found dead beside the tracks at Mughalsarai station, having left Lucknow by night train. The CBI concludes he was killed by two petty thieves; a court acquits them of murder and convicts one of theft, and the Y. V. Chandrachud inquiry (1970) finds no political motive. Balraj Madhok and others in the party never accepted this, and calls to reopen the case continue. The station is renamed after him in 2018.

events.title: 1971: Indira's landslide
events.summary: Against Indira Gandhi's 'Garibi Hatao' landslide the Jana Sangh slips to 22 seats.

events.title: Advani becomes president; Madhok expelled
events.summary: L. K. Advani becomes president of the Jana Sangh. Former president Balraj Madhok, who attacked the party's drift, is expelled.

events.title: The Jana Sangh joins the JP movement
events.summary: Jayaprakash Narayan leads student protests in Bihar and Gujarat against corruption and Indira Gandhi. The Jana Sangh and RSS throw their organisation behind 'Total Revolution', and JP calls them a force for change.

events.title: The Emergency
events.summary: Indira Gandhi declares an Emergency. Vajpayee, Advani and thousands of Jana Sangh and RSS workers are jailed, and the RSS is banned for a second time.

events.title: The Jana Sangh merges into the Janata Party
events.summary: To defeat Indira Gandhi the opposition unites. The Jana Sangh dissolves itself into the new Janata Party with the Congress (O), the Bharatiya Lok Dal and the socialists — the Jana Sangh's 'JP' years.

events.title: Janata wins; Vajpayee and Advani in office
events.summary: The Janata Party sweeps the post-Emergency election and Morarji Desai becomes the first non-Congress Prime Minister. Former Jana Sangh members make up the largest bloc of its MPs; Vajpayee becomes Foreign Minister and Advani Information Minister.

events.title: Vajpayee speaks Hindi at the UN
events.summary: Foreign Minister Vajpayee becomes the first to address the UN General Assembly in Hindi.

events.title: Dual membership splits the Janata Party
events.summary: Socialists led by Madhu Limaye demand that former Jana Sangh members quit the RSS. The quarrel and Charan Singh's defection bring down Desai's government; Indira Gandhi sweeps back in January 1980.

events.title: The BJP is founded
events.summary: Expelled from the Janata Party over dual membership, the former Jana Sangh members found the Bharatiya Janata Party in Delhi with Vajpayee as president and the lotus as its symbol. It declares 'Gandhian socialism' as its creed.

events.title: 1984: just 2 seats
events.summary: After Indira Gandhi's assassination, the sympathy wave gives Rajiv Gandhi's Congress 404 seats. The BJP wins only 2 — Hanamkonda in Andhra Pradesh and Mehsana in Gujarat. Even Vajpayee loses in Gwalior.

events.title: Advani takes over, back to Integral Humanism
events.summary: Advani replaces Vajpayee as president. The party drops Gandhian socialism for Integral Humanism and moves closer to the RSS and the VHP's Ayodhya campaign.

events.title: Palampur resolution on Ayodhya
events.summary: Meeting in Palampur, the BJP formally backs the demand for a Ram temple at the site of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, making the Ram Janmabhoomi movement its central cause.

events.title: 1989: 85 seats; propping up V. P. Singh
events.summary: The BJP jumps to 85 seats. With the Left, it backs from outside the National Front government of V. P. Singh, whose Janata Dal had been formed in 1988 — a different party from the BJP's Janata Party past.

events.title: Advani's Ram Rath Yatra
events.summary: Advani sets out from Somnath in a Toyota fitted out as a chariot, bound for Ayodhya. Bihar's chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav arrests him at Samastipur on 23 October; the BJP withdraws support and V. P. Singh's government falls.

events.title: 1991: main opposition; Uttar Pradesh won
events.summary: The BJP wins 120 seats to become the main opposition, and forms its first government in Uttar Pradesh under Kalyan Singh.

events.title: Babri Masjid demolished
events.summary: Kar sevaks at a rally attended by Advani and other leaders tear down the 16th-century Babri Masjid. Riots kill around 2,000 across India; the BJP state governments are dismissed.

events.title: Vajpayee's 13-day government
events.summary: The BJP becomes the largest party with 161 seats and Vajpayee is sworn in as Prime Minister. Unable to find allies, he resigns after 13 days.

events.title: Vajpayee PM at the head of the NDA
events.summary: With 182 seats and allies grouped into the National Democratic Alliance, Vajpayee returns as Prime Minister.

events.title: Pokhran-II nuclear tests
events.summary: Two months into office, Vajpayee's government conducts five nuclear tests at Pokhran and declares India a nuclear weapons state. Pakistan replies with its own tests.

events.title: Bus to Lahore
events.summary: Vajpayee rides the inaugural Delhi–Lahore bus and signs the Lahore Declaration with Nawaz Sharif.

events.title: Government falls by one vote
events.summary: After Jayalalithaa's AIADMK pulls out, the Vajpayee government loses a confidence vote 269 to 270.

events.title: The Kargil War
events.summary: Pakistani troops occupying heights near Kargil are pushed back after two months of fighting, while Vajpayee leads a caretaker government.

events.title: 1999: the NDA wins a full term
events.summary: The NDA wins a majority and Vajpayee begins the first full term of a non-Congress Prime Minister, with Advani as Home Minister and later Deputy Prime Minister.

events.title: Three new states
events.summary: The Vajpayee government creates Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand out of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

events.title: Modi becomes Gujarat chief minister
events.summary: Narendra Modi, an RSS pracharak turned BJP organiser, replaces Keshubhai Patel as chief minister of Gujarat. He holds the post for 13 years.

events.title: Godhra and the Gujarat riots
events.summary: A fire on a train carrying kar sevaks back from Ayodhya kills 59 at Godhra. In the communal violence that follows across Gujarat over 1,000 people are killed, most of them Muslims; Modi's government is accused of failing to stop it.

events.title: 'India Shining' fails
events.summary: Despite its upbeat 'India Shining' campaign the NDA loses. The BJP falls to 138 seats and Congress forms the UPA government under Manmohan Singh.

events.title: Advani's Jinnah remarks
events.summary: Visiting Jinnah's mausoleum in Karachi, Advani calls him 'secular'. The RSS is furious and Advani steps down as president; Rajnath Singh succeeds him.

events.title: 2009: Advani's campaign falls short
events.summary: With Advani as its prime-ministerial candidate, the BJP drops to 116 seats and the UPA returns.

events.title: Modi named for Prime Minister
events.summary: Over Advani's objections, the BJP names Narendra Modi as its prime-ministerial candidate.

events.title: 2014: the first BJP majority
events.summary: The BJP wins 282 seats, the first single-party Lok Sabha majority since 1984 and the first ever for a party other than Congress. Modi is sworn in as Prime Minister on 26 May.

events.title: Amit Shah takes over the party
events.summary: Modi's closest aide Amit Shah becomes BJP president and expands the party into the north-east and beyond, claiming over 100 million members.

events.title: Demonetisation
events.summary: Modi announces that ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes — 86% of the cash in circulation — cease to be legal tender at midnight.

events.title: Goods and Services Tax
events.summary: A single national GST replaces a web of central and state taxes.

events.title: Vajpayee dies
events.summary: Atal Bihari Vajpayee, founder-president of the BJP and its first Prime Minister, dies aged 93.

events.title: 2019: 303 seats
events.summary: The BJP increases its majority to 303 seats with 37% of the vote. Amit Shah becomes Home Minister.

events.title: Article 370 revoked
events.summary: The government ends Jammu and Kashmir's special status and splits it into two union territories — the cause Mookerjee died for in 1953.
events.wiki: Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir

events.title: Supreme Court Ayodhya verdict
events.summary: The Supreme Court awards the disputed site in Ayodhya for a Ram temple and directs that land be given elsewhere for a mosque.

events.title: Citizenship (Amendment) Act
events.summary: Parliament passes the CAA, offering faster citizenship to non-Muslim refugees from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. It sets off months of nationwide protest.

events.title: J. P. Nadda becomes president
events.summary: J. P. Nadda succeeds Amit Shah as BJP president.

events.title: The Ram Mandir is consecrated
events.summary: Modi leads the consecration of the Ram temple in Ayodhya, built on the site of the Babri Masjid — the goal of the Palampur resolution 35 years earlier.

events.title: 2024: majority lost, coalition kept
events.summary: The BJP falls to 240 seats, short of a majority, and relies on NDA allies — Chandrababu Naidu's Telugu Desam and Nitish Kumar's Janata Dal (United). Modi is sworn in for a third term on 9 June.

events.title: Nitin Nabin becomes president
events.summary: Nitin Nabin, 45, is elected unopposed as BJP president, succeeding J. P. Nadda as the youngest leader in the party's history.

events.title: 75 years since the Jana Sangh
events.summary: The BJP marks the 75th anniversary of Mookerjee's Bharatiya Jana Sangh, the party's first incarnation.

events.title: Calcutta South-East: Mookerjee's own seat
events.summary: Mookerjee wins 45% of the vote (65,026) against Congress's Mriganka Mohan Sur (30%) and the Communist Sadhan Gupta (22%). His name, his 1950 resignation over the Nehru–Liaquat Pact and the East Bengal Hindu refugees of south Calcutta carry the seat while Congress and the CPI split the rest. After his death, Gupta wins the 1953 by-election.
events.wiki: Calcutta South East Lok Sabha constituency

events.title: Midnapore–Jhargram: Durga Charan Banerjee
events.summary: In this two-member seat (one general, one reserved for Scheduled Tribes) Durga Charan Banerjee, a Midnapore-born criminal lawyer known for Ramakrishna Mission work, tops the poll with 1,51,494 votes. Congress is split by the breakaway Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party, which takes over 1.6 lakh votes, and wins only the reserved seat.

events.title: Chittor: Trivedi beats Manikya Lal Verma
events.summary: Uma Shankar Trivedi, a barrister who left Congress in 1951, defeats Manikya Lal Verma, the Praja Mandal leader who had fought the Maharana of Mewar and led the United State of Rajasthan, by 6,599 votes (47% to 41%) on a 28% turnout. 1952 is a bad year for Congress in Rajasthan, where former princes and jagirdars rally voters against it; a Socialist takes another 13%.

events.title: Mookerjee dies in detention in Srinagar
events.summary: Held for six weeks in a cottage outside Srinagar, Mookerjee falls ill and dies in hospital on 23 June, officially of a heart attack. His mother Jogmaya Devi writes to Nehru demanding an independent inquiry; Nehru replies that he has looked into it and sees no mystery. No inquiry is ever held, and the Jana Sangh and BJP have called it a conspiracy ever since. The party loses its founder 20 months after its birth.

events.title: Massacre at an RSS shakha in Moga
events.summary: Khalistani militants open fire on a morning RSS shakha in a park in Moga, Punjab, killing 25 people. It is the deadliest attack on the Sangh during the Punjab insurgency.

events.title: Tika Lal Taploo shot in Srinagar
events.summary: Tika Lal Taploo, a lawyer and vice-president of the BJP in Jammu and Kashmir, is shot outside his home by JKLF militants. He is the first in a series of targeted killings of Kashmiri Pandits that leads to their mass flight from the valley in 1990.

events.title: Police fire on kar sevaks in Ayodhya
events.summary: With Advani under arrest, kar sevaks try to reach the Babri Masjid. Uttar Pradesh police under Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav open fire. Official figures put the dead at under 20; the VHP and BJP claimed many more. The deaths become a rallying cry for the temple movement.

events.title: Coimbatore bombings target Advani
events.summary: Bombs explode across Coimbatore minutes before Advani is due to address an election rally there; 58 people are killed. The Islamist group Al Umma is found responsible and its founder S. A. Basha is convicted.

events.title: K. T. Jayakrishnan killed in his classroom
events.summary: Jayakrishnan, a schoolteacher and state vice-president of the BJP's youth wing, is hacked to death in front of his pupils at a school in Kannur district. CPI(M) workers are convicted; most are later acquitted on appeal. In Kannur's long cycle of RSS–CPI(M) violence, workers on both sides have been killed and convicted.

events.title: Haren Pandya shot in Ahmedabad
events.summary: Haren Pandya, Gujarat's former home minister, who had fallen out with Narendra Modi, is found shot dead in his car on a morning walk. Twelve men are convicted in 2007; the Gujarat High Court acquits them in 2011, and the Supreme Court restores the convictions in 2019. His father and widow said the killing was political and the investigation flawed.

events.title: Pramod Mahajan shot by his brother
events.summary: Pramod Mahajan, the BJP general secretary seen as Vajpayee and Advani's heir, is shot at his Mumbai home by his younger brother Pravin and dies 12 days later. It is a family quarrel, not a political killing; Pravin is sentenced to life.

events.title: V. Ramesh killed in Salem
events.summary: V. Ramesh, a chartered accountant and the Tamil Nadu BJP's state general secretary, is hacked to death outside his home in Salem, after a series of attacks on Hindu Munnani and BJP figures in western Tamil Nadu.

events.title: Gopinath Munde dies in a car crash
events.summary: A week after joining Modi's cabinet as rural development minister, Gopinath Munde is killed when a car hits his at a Delhi crossing. His family and supporters ask for a CBI probe; the CBI concludes it was an accident.

events.title: Waseem Bari and family shot in Bandipora
events.summary: Militants shoot dead BJP district leader Sheikh Waseem Bari, his father and his brother outside their shop in Bandipora, Kashmir. Through 2020 militants target BJP panches and workers in the valley.

events.title: Post-poll violence in West Bengal
events.summary: After the Trinamool Congress wins the West Bengal assembly election, BJP workers are attacked across the state and several are killed. The Calcutta High Court orders the CBI to investigate the murders and rapes, saying the state police cannot be relied on.

events.title: Ranjith Sreenivasan killed in Alappuzha
events.summary: Hours after SDPI leader K. S. Shan is killed, allegedly by RSS workers, a gang hacks BJP leader Ranjith Sreenivasan to death at his home in front of his family. In 2024 a court sentences 15 PFI–SDPI members to death.

events.title: Praveen Nettaru killed; PFI banned
events.summary: BJP youth worker Praveen Nettaru is hacked to death outside his shop at Bellare, Dakshina Kannada. The NIA charges members of the Popular Front of India, and in September the government bans the PFI for five years.
